claim.pdf_says:
NOTE    The VALIDATE facility is an obsolete feature.

Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in this facility will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove it from the next revision.  [both paragraphs are set in the smaller NOTE type face, visibly smaller than the surrounding body text - i.e. the second paragraph is a continuation of the NOTE, not body text]
claim.markdown_says:
NOTE The VALIDATE facility is an obsolete feature.

Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in this facility will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove it from the next revision.
claim.why_it_matters: The second paragraph is rendered as ordinary body prose, so its binding to the NOTE is lost - a sub-item detached from its parent. Impact is cosmetic only: Annex D is informative in its entirety, so nothing normative turns on it.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED - the claim's observation about the PDF is accurate, but it describes a pure typography difference that the transcription does not encode anywhere, so it is not a content discrepancy.

WHAT THE PRINTED PAGE ACTUALLY SHOWS (spec_p1171.png, 2550x3300 @300dpi, printed folio 1141). I measured first-glyph cap-height per text line: body line 'The validate facility provides...' T = 31 px; body line 'The VALIDATE statement can be used...' T = 31 px; 'NOTE  The VALIDATE facility is an obsolete feature.' N = 27 px; 'Unlike other obsolete features...' U = 27 px; its runover 'of standard COBOL and before...' = 28 px. So the NOTE line and the 'Unlike...' paragraph are both set at ~87% of the body cap-height. The claim's premise is CORRECT: the 'Unlike...' paragraph is in the smaller NOTE face, not the body face. All paragraphs share the same left margin (x=335-336) and the same right measure, so there is no indent distinction either.

WHY IT IS STILL NOT A DISCREPANCY:

(1) The text is verbatim identical. Every word, in the same order, with the same paragraph break between the NOTE sentence and the 'Unlike...' paragraph - the PDF prints them as two separated paragraphs exactly as the markdown does. Nothing is missing, added, reordered, or altered. The only textual delta is whitespace collapse ('NOTE    The' -> 'NOTE The'), which is line-formatting, an explicit rejection ground.

(2) The difference is formatting only - font size - which the rejection criteria list by name. Point size is not content.

(3) The transcription has NO note-typography convention to violate, document-wide. specs/ISO_COBOL.md renders every ISO NOTE as a plain paragraph beginning with the literal word 'NOTE' (25 occurrences of 'NOTE    The ' alone, plus numbered 'NOTE 1'/'NOTE 2' forms). There is zero italic/small markup ('*NOTE' appears 0 times in the whole file), and the 374 blockquote lines are used for figure notes and page footnotes, not for ISO NOTE elements. Crucially, the markdown does not distinguish the NOTE's OWN first line from body prose either - it too is plain text. So the 'binding' the claim says was lost was never encoded for any NOTE in the document. Accepting this finding would require filing an identical finding against every NOTE on every page, which is a transcription-format property, not a per-page defect.

(4) The mis-binding does not survive reading. 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in THIS FACILITY will be reevaluated...' anaphorically resolves to the VALIDATE facility named in the immediately preceding NOTE sentence; the elaboration reads as an elaboration of the note whether or not it is set in 8pt. Meaning is unchanged.

(5) The kind label is wrong on its own terms. Nothing is 'misplaced-content': the paragraph sits in exactly the position the PDF puts it, between the NOTE and 'The VALIDATE statement can be used to perform validation...'.

(6) The claim itself concedes the impact is nil - Annex D is headed '(informative)' in the transcription (confirmed: '## Annex D\n(informative)'), so nothing normative turns on it under any reading.

No ledger entry warranted.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The claim's reading of the PDF is accurate - measured cap-heights confirm the 'Unlike other obsolete features...' paragraph is set at ~87% of body size, matching the NOTE line and therefore belonging to the NOTE - but the markdown reproduces both paragraphs verbatim, in order, with the same paragraph break. The sole delta is point size, a typographic attribute the transcription encodes for no NOTE anywhere in ISO_COBOL.md (the NOTE's own first line is likewise plain prose). This is a global plain-text transcription property, not a page-1171 defect, and it changes no meaning in an annex that is informative in its entirety.
